name: ZeroClaw
vibe_summary: A single-binary Rust agent runtime that positions itself as the lean, self-owned alternative to OpenClaw — 30+ channels, ~20 LLM providers, and a plugin system in one deployable artifact. Extremely active development with a security-hardening focus (OIDC, plugin admission, opt-in browser automation) and a strong 'you own the machine' philosophy.
best_for: Users who want a lightweight, low-RAM agent on small hardware (NAS, Raspberry Pi, old laptops)
Self-hosters who want one binary instead of a multi-service stack
Operators needing many chat channels (Telegram, Discord, Matrix, email) from one runtime
avoid_if: You want a polished GUI/dashboard experience out of the box
You need a mature, stable plugin ecosystem with third-party extensions
You prefer managed cloud hosting over running your own binary
openclaw_advantages: Dramatically lower resource footprint — single Rust binary runnable in tens of MB of RAM
Simpler deployment: one install script, no orchestrated service stack
Runs on constrained hardware (ARM NAS, Raspberry Pi, Android) where OpenClaw is impractical
Explicit local-first ownership model: your keys, your workspace, your machine
openclaw_disadvantages: No equivalent of OpenClaw's Control UI dashboard and Canvas features
Younger project (v0.8.x) with pre-1.0 stability and frequent breaking-change risk
Plugin/component system still under active construction with admission bugs being fixed
Smaller ecosystem of ready-made skills and integrations compared to OpenClaw
confidence_summary: Strong evidence from README, release data, and multiple independent ecosystem digests confirming ZeroClaw's positioning as a lightweight OpenClaw alternative. Uncertainty remains around multi-user support and real-world plugin maturity since the plugin system is visibly mid-refactor in recent commits.

overview_markdown:
ZeroClaw is an agent runtime written in Rust and distributed as a single binary, built around four ownership principles: you own the agent, the data, and the machine it runs on. It connects to roughly 20 LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and others), reaches users through 30+ channels including Discord, Telegram, Matrix, email, voice, and webhooks, and acts through tools such as shell, browser, HTTP, hardware, and custom MCP servers. Installation is a one-line curl script or a prebuilt Windows binary, followed by an interactive quickstart.

Architecturally, it contrasts sharply with OpenClaw's heavier stack: instead of a multi-service deployment with a Control UI, ZeroClaw is a single configurable process designed to run anywhere — from a $200 ARM NAS to Android devices — with a memory footprint measured in tens of megabytes. Recent commits show heavy investment in correctness and security hardening: an OIDC token-verification provider, plugin component admission with exact payload byte validation, opt-in gating for full browser automation, deterministic tool-spec ordering for prompt-cache stability, and token accounting on history-trim events.

The trade-off is maturity. At v0.8.5, ZeroClaw is pre-1.0 with a plugin system still being actively rebuilt, and it lacks OpenClaw's dashboard, Canvas, and polished multi-agent UI. It is best understood as the infrastructure-first, resource-frugal member of the Claw family: ideal for self-hosters who want an always-on assistant on cheap hardware, less ideal for users who want a batteries-included graphical experience.
